claims: The Artemis program is a series of NASA-led missions returning humans to the Moon for long-term exploration.
Artemis I successfully completed an uncrewed test flight on November 16, 2022.
Artemis I tested the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft.
Artemis I orbited the Moon.
Artemis II is targeted for April 2026.
Artemis II is the first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft to orbit the Moon.
Artemis II will last ~10 days.
The Artemis II crew will test life-support and emergency systems.
Artemis III is targeted for mid-2027.
Artemis III is targeted to land the first astronauts on the lunar South Pole.
Artemis III will include the first woman and first person of color among those astronauts.
Artemis III will use a SpaceX HLS (Human Landing System).
Artemis IV is targeted for early 2028.
Artemis IV is a second crewed landing mission.
Artemis IV will carry out construction of the Gateway.
The Gateway is an orbiting lunar space station.
Artemis V is targeted for late 2028.
Artemis V involves further lunar surface missions to build a permanent base.
Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, Jeremy Hansen.
Artemis II launch uses SLS from Kennedy Space Center, FL, placing Orion in Earth orbit.
Artemis II includes translunar injection where engines fire to send Orion toward the Moon.
Artemis II includes a lunar flyby where the crew loops around the far side of the Moon.
Artemis II return involves a slingshot maneuver and splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
